speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me how long you have had these symptoms and if there is any pain when you urinate?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. The relief of discomfort after voiding and dyspareunia are concerning for interstitial cystitis or a bladder infection. To differentiate these, have you noticed any blood in your urine, and do you have any fevers or chills? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Color Clear, pH 6.7, Specific Gravity 1.010, Protein 1+, Glucose Negative, Ketones Negative, Blood Negative, Nitrite Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Negative, WBC 0/hpf, Squamous Epithelial Cells 2/hpf, Bacteria None

speaker: Doctor
text: A previous doctor suspected a urinary tract infection, but given your 5-month duration, relief with voiding, and painful intercourse, this may be interstitial cystitis or a chronic pelvic pain syndrome. I need to rule out infection first, so I have already ordered a urinalysis and culture; have you noticed any visible blood in your urine? REQUEST IMAGES: Bladder_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Significant for bipolar disorder, currently managed with lithium. Social history: Married and sexually active with her husband. No significant alcohol, tobacco, or recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lithium-induced nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
